title: Baxter launches Connex 360 Vital Signs Monitor in Qatar to advance digital healthcare
summary: The launch aligns with Qatar’s healthcare transformation agenda under Qatar National Vision 2030 and the National Health Strategy 2024–2030, known as Health for All.

contentHtml:
QATAR—Baxter International has launched its Welch Allyn Connex 360 Vital Signs Monitor in Qatar, introducing connected patient monitoring technology to support faster clinical assessments, improve documentation and help healthcare teams identify deteriorating patients earlier.

The launch event in Doha brought together healthcare leaders, clinicians and IT specialists from the Ministry of Interior, Hamad Medical Corporation, The View Hospital, Military Medical City Hospital and Sidra Medicine.

Attendees participated in live demonstrations of the monitor’s automated documentation and Early Warning Score capabilities.

Supporting Qatar’s digital health strategy

The launch aligns with Qatar’s healthcare transformation agenda under Qatar National Vision 2030 and the National Health Strategy 2024–2030, known as Health for All.

The strategy aims to strengthen an integrated health system focused on clinical quality, sustainability and innovation.

Qatar’s continued investment in digital health infrastructure and interoperable systems is creating opportunities for connected medical devices that integrate with hospital information systems.

These technologies can help healthcare providers improve access to patient information, reduce administrative workloads and support more consistent clinical decision-making.

Automating vital signs monitoring

Vital signs measurements, including blood pressure, temperature, pulse rate and blood oxygen saturation, are routinely collected in hospitals and other healthcare settings.

However, manual recording can consume clinical staff time and introduce transcription errors, particularly in busy environments where timely, accurate information is essential.

The Connex 360 monitor captures a complete set of vital signs in less than a minute and automatically transfers the readings to hospital information systems, reducing the need for manual data entry.

Its configurable Early Warning Score protocols help clinical teams recognise signs of patient deterioration and prioritise further assessment.

By combining automated measurements with electronic documentation, the system is designed to support earlier intervention and more efficient clinical workflows.

“Healthcare systems across Qatar continue to embrace innovation that improves the quality and efficiency of care,” said Beata Karasinska, general manager for Central Eastern Europe, the Middle East, Türkiye and Africa at Baxter.

Karasinska said the company was introducing Connex 360 to help healthcare providers access timely patient information, streamline workflows and spend more time caring for patients while protecting sensitive data.

She also linked the launch to Baxter’s long-term commitment to Qatar and its mission to save and sustain lives.

Data security and connected care

As hospitals expand their use of connected medical devices, safeguarding patient information remains a critical requirement.

Connex 360 uses end-to-end encryption and certificate-based authentication to protect data as it moves between the bedside and hospital systems.

The launch builds on Baxter’s Welch Allyn patient monitoring portfolio as the company continues to develop connected care technologies.

For healthcare providers, integrating automated monitoring with existing digital infrastructure offers a way to reduce documentation burdens while strengthening information flow across clinical teams.

Successful implementation will depend on reliable system integration, appropriate staff training and robust data protection practices.
